To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the radiosensitization of hypoxic Chinese hamsters cells by 2-nitronidazoles is due to the presence of the nitro group and the imidazole ring; 2. the sensitization is not a result of the formation of free radicals, but is probably related to the reduction of the nitro to hydroxylamino group and the subsequent re-oxidation; 3. the sensitization efficiency is related to the ease with which the

1) the sensitizing efficiency of a 2-nitrimidazole is increased by substituting it with groups carrying basic substituents, 2) the increase in radiosensitization efficiency is not associated with an increase in the aerobic toxicity of the compound and 3) the increase in sensitization is associated with an increase of the compound in the hypoxic cell fraction.
The radiosensitizing activity of nitroimidazoles can be increased by the introduction of basic substituants into the side chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a series of nitroimidazole derivatives which are capable of sensitizing hypoxic cells to the cytotoxic effects of ionizing radiation.
the structure-activity relationships of hypoxic cell sensitizers.
the design and synthesis of nitroimidazole derivatives with enhanced hypoxic cell sensitization efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the basic substituents studied in this paper are not useful as hypoxic cell sensitizers.
, in general, the presence of a basic group in the sidechain of a nitroimidazole increases the hypoxic cell sensitization efficiency and reduces the aerobic toxicity.
the introduction of basic groups to the sidechains of 2-nitrimidazoles can result in a substantial increase in radiosensitization efficiency without an increase in the aerobic toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important factor for sensitization efficiency is the redox property of the compound.
, of a series of 2-nitrimidazoles, 1-(2-nitro-imidazol-1-yl)alkylamine derivatives are the most promising as hypoxic cell sensitizers.

the sensitizing activity in vitro of 2-nitrimidazoles is not related simply to their lipophilicity, but that the presence of an electron-withdrawing substituent on the imidazole ring is essential for sensitization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
basic substituents on nitroimidazole moieties can enhance radiosensitization efficiency in vitro without increasing aerobic toxicity.
basic substituents can be used to increase the efficiency of 2-nitrimidazoles without increasing the cytotoxicity of the compounds.
basic substituents can be used in the sidechain of a 2-nitrimidazole to increase the radiosensitizing activity without increasing cytotoxicity.
